name: no-address
description:
REGRESSION LOCK for the hardcoded loopback placeholder. build_assets used to open every iteration with `ips = ["127.0.0.1"]` and pass it to every network_interface call, so each Netskope asset was built with an interface carrying the loopback address. Verified against the scanner: network_interface(ips=["127.0.0.1"], mac=None) really does return NetworkInterface(ipv4_addresses=["127.0.0.1"], mac_address=None) -- the placeholder was on the interface, and it disappeared only because the platform's NormalizeAddress rejects loopback one layer later. Correctness that rests on a filter in another component is not correctness.

Removing the literal exposes two aborts this scenario pins. network_interface returns None when nothing usable survives, and networkInterfaces=[None] aborts the entire run: DEV-0002 reports no MAC at all, and DEV-0003 reports a MAC string the platform cannot read, so both must produce an asset with NO interface rather than a None one. DEV-0004 sends mac_addresses as an explicit null, which .get(k, []) returns as None and which only `or []` survives. DEV-0005 comes last and must still be emitted, which is what proves nothing aborted along the way.

Skips namespaced_ids: netskope uses the bare nsdeviceuid as the foreign id, with no tenant scope, so two Netskope tenants imported into one runZero instance would collide. Not this scenario's defect.
